summary: Lyft Engineering explains PrimeTime, Lyft’s dynamic pricing algorithm, as a system for maintaining marketplace balance in real time when rider demand and driver supply fluctuate. The post describes iterations of the algorithm that use availability targets, price-response modeling, ETA targeting, online machine learning, and constrained optimization across networks of local markets. Lyft frames price increases as a way to suppress demand during undersupply and improve rider and driver service levels.

summary: The NBER working paper audits identical trips on Uber and Lyft and documents price dispersion across the two platforms. It finds that only 16.1 percent of consumers who open one app also open the other and estimates that comparison-shopping frictions increase platforms’ gross booking volume by more than $300 million annually in New York City alone. The source is useful for Lyft because it provides empirical evidence of price differences and low price-comparison behavior in the ride-hailing market.

summary: Senator Sherrod Brown wrote to Lyft CEO David Risher seeking transparency about Lyft’s dynamic or surge pricing. The letter says Lyft has long used dynamic pricing to set fares based on consumer demand and asks how Lyft sets and changes ride prices, what data it uses, whether purchase history, browsing history, device or battery level are used, and whether Lyft estimates each consumer’s highest willingness to pay. It also asks how Lyft prevents pricing algorithms from discriminating based on protected classes.

summary: The Washington Post compared 80 Uber and Lyft ride quotes in San Francisco and reports that base fares differed by about 14 percent across apps, with neither app consistently cheaper. The article says Lyft attributed price variation to separate marketplaces and different pricing approaches for on-demand service conditions that change minute to minute, denied that base prices are personalized, and said dynamic rates reflect location, demand, estimated time and distance, traffic, and driver availability. Lyft also welcomed rider comparison shopping as a way to save money.
